singular noun

in grammar

also singular number, in the singular

classical

Quint. 1.5.42: in quibus nōs singulārem ac plūrālem habēmus
Varr. LL 10.54 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 221, 248

singulāris, singulāre

Declension on Wiktionary

singular, of one

numerus singulāris, the singular number; numerī singulāris, in the singular (Traupman 238); adverb singulāriter, in the singular (Quint. 1.5.16; Traupman 248). Latin, Quintilian notes, has singular and plural where Greek also has a dual.

Examples

  • nōn aliō vitiōsa sunt, quam quod plūrālia singulāriter et singulāria plūrāliter efferuntur

    they are wrong only in this, that plurals are spoken in the singular and singulars in the pluralQuint. 1.5.16

  • Cujus est numerī? — Numerī singulāris.

    What number is it? — Singular.Traupman 238

  • singulāriter

    in the singularTraupman 379

See also plural, number, noun.

SourcesLewis & Short: singularis
